title: Signal Limn & Request Plotter — Customer feedback synthesis (Nov 2027)
content:
TL;DR:
A compact synthesis of field signals from the past 10 weeks focused on runtime economics and reliability asks. Goal: produce a short, prioritized runway of experiments and delivery bets (fast wins, 1–3mo, and gated enterprise work). This note introduces a simple scoring "plotter" that maps customer pain (severity + frequency) against implementation cost to help engineering prioritize small patches vs platform changes.

Background/context:
- Trigger: spike of incoming customer requests asking for more observable KV-cache behavior, safer fallback routing, and per-route cost controls. Several request threads converged (FinraBank, EduSolve, ComplyAI) with overlapping asks.
- Why this matters: customers are optimizing unit economics and reliability simultaneously; small changes (KV metrics, route-by-cost toggles) appear to have outsized short-term ROI.

How the Plotter works (quick heuristic):
- Score_request = (Severity * Frequency * Customer_weight) / Estimated_engineering_cost
- Severity: 1–5 (customer impact on availability/latency or compliance risk).
- Frequency: observed signal counts per week (normalized).
- Customer_weight: 1.2 for enterprise, 0.9 for mid-market, 0.6 for startup (reflects ARR influence).
- Cost: T-shirt: S/M/L mapped to 1/3/8 (approx weeks of engineering + platform integration).
- Output: cluster into 3 lanes: Quick Wins (score > 2.5), Strategic Bets (1.0–2.5), Heavy Lifts (<1.0).

High-impact asks surfaced (grouped):
1) KV-cache visibility and eviction telemetry (Quick Win candidate)
   - Pain: customers report opaque token accounting when prefix reuse occurs; hard to debug per-route cost anomalies.
   - Asks: per-request KV-hit/miss headers, dashboard slice for KV hit-rate by model and route, opt-in logging for eviction reasons.
   - Example vignette: FinraBank saw a 40% token cost variance week-over-week; engineering traced it to unexpected cache churn across multi-tenant pools.
   - Rough estimate: S (1 week) + small dashboard tile -> 4–8% unit-cost reduction for affected customers; high debugging ROI.

2) Route-by-cost and fallback policy primitives (Strategic Bet)
   - Pain: large customers want rules to route low-latency traffic to premium pools and background/budgeted traffic to cheaper quantized variants.
   - Asks: declarative policy layer (latency vs cost thresholds), soft-fallback mapping (automated downgrade when reserved capacity full).
   - Example vignette: EduSolve needs 99.9% interactivity for student-facing chat; back-office analytics can use cheaper models but currently share throttles.
   - Rough estimate: M (3 weeks) + config UI changes. Significant recurring savings for customers that shard traffic.

3) Per-route token caps and early-stop nudges (Quick Win)
   - Pain: runaway prompting loops in customer workflows cause token spikes and manual escalations.
   - Asks: server-side per-route budget guards + configurable early-stop threshold with friendly error messages and telemetry.
   - Cost: S. Fast to instrument in proxy layer and enforce with sidecar.

4) Canary-in-rotation + A/B baseline regression detector (Medium/Heavy)
   - Pain: model rollouts cause subtle quality regressions; customers want automatic rollback triggers based on representative eval prompts.
   - Asks: tie rollouts to prompt-sets and perf regressions; automated canary pause/rollback on quality drop or latency spike.
   - Cost: L. Needs eval infra integration and policy engine surface.

Customer vignettes (short):
- FinraBank (enterprise): required cryptographic KMS integration + strict audit trails; urgent visibility into cache evictions so auditors can reconcile token charges. Proposed near-term: KV-hit header + audit log entry (owner: eng-infra).
- EduSolve (mid-market): student-facing app; wants per-route SLA that maps to lower cost offline grading workloads. Proposed: route tags + route budget caps + routing policy (owner: product-hosted-api + eng-routing).
- ComplyAI (startup): hit repeated quality cliffs after model swap; they'd accept slower but cheaper fallback during load spikes. Proposed: a fallback mapping UI and default policy templates (owner: eng-serving-runtime).

Quick wins (<= 2 weeks):
- Emit KV-hit/miss header (S)
- Add per-route token cap flag and error code (S)
- Small dashboard card showing KV hit-rate for top 10 routes (S)
- Slack probe: collect 5 recent cases where evictions correlate with cost spikes (owner: CS ops)

Medium-term (1–3 months):
- Routing policy primitives + basic UI for cost-vs-latency toggles (M)
- Canary-eval hook prototype that runs a small prompt set against candidate model variant (M)
- Cost simulation tool for customers: estimate monthly savings by applying quantized model to a traffic slice (M)

Longer/higher-risk (>3mo):
- Full rollout automation with automatic rollback tied to evals and customer prompts (L)
- Enterprise-grade audit trail and per-tenant KV eviction reconciliation that meets regulated audit controls (L)

Open risks and questions (for triage):
- Security/compliance: storing eviction reasons and KV metadata may leak PII if not redacted. Need sec review and KMS patterns.
- Data volume: KV hit telemetry at request granularity will increase observability costs. Explore sampling + aggregated counters.
- UX: customers want a simple toggle; platform owners fear combinatorial explosion of policies. Consider templates and sane defaults.

Proposed next steps (this week):
- CS to run a 7-day signal audit: pull 30 example sessions across the three vignette customers and tag where KV evictions or model fallbacks caused cost anomaly (owner: Asha + Diego).
- Engineering spike: implement KV-hit header prototype + minimal dashboard card (owner: eng-infra: Priya) target: demo 2027-11-20.
- Product: draft routing-policy UX with 3 preset templates (Strict low-latency, Balanced, Cost-first) and circulate for feedback (owner: product-hosted-api).

Owners and suggested communication cadence:
- Weekly sync: 30m triage (CS + eng infra + product) until prototype complete.
- Decision gate: evaluate quick wins results 2 weeks after prototype (metrics: mean token cost for pilot customers, KV hit-rate change, customer satisfaction).

Notes to self / things to capture in follow-ups:
- Capture one reproducible FinraBank session with cache-churn timeline (timestamps + pool mapping).
- Create a small sample prompt-set for EduSolve to use when testing canary fallbacks.
- Check with security for PII redaction plan before enabling per-request verbose telemetry.

Unresolved questions for leadership: 
- Should we expose per-route 'cost tiers' that map to billing plans or keep it strictly control-only (no billing change)? (ops + finance input needed)
- What is the minimum acceptable sample rate for KV telemetry to be actionable but cost-limited?

Appendix (quick heuristics):
- Suggested default plotter thresholds: Quick > 2.5, Strategic 1–2.5, Heavy <1.0 (calibrated on 20 historical asks).
- Example calculation: FinraBank severity=4, frequency=6/week (normalized 1.2), cust_weight=1.2, cost=S(1)-> Score=(4*1.2*1.2)/1 = 5.76 -> Quick Win.

End of note.

-- Asha (CS)
summary: Compact synthesis with a triage heuristic and prioritized runway; recommends KV-hit visibility and per-route budgets as fast wins, routing policy primitives and canary-eval integration as strategic bets, with clear owners and short next steps.
